tier_reason: README prints first-party decodebenchmark output (benchmarks/decodebenchmark.cpp) for scalarcodec vs AVXDictCODEC/AVX512DictCODEC with gcc 5.3.0 and Makefile flags -O3 -march=native, but hardware is only 'Skylake' and an 'UNKNOWN' Knights Landing with no CPU model, so it falls short of A; baseline is the authors' own scalar decoder.

corrections.caveats: Baseline is the authors' own scalar decoder (scalarcodec), not a widely used external incumbent, so baseline_in_list is false. The gain shrinks as the dictionary outgrows cache: Skylake size 65536 scalar 7.14 vs AVX2 fast 5.18 cycles per value, size 1048576 11.85 vs 8.47; the AVX2 path stays faster at every listed size (the earlier note that it was slower at size 8192 was a misreading: size 8192 is 4.35 vs 2.28). README states the code is a demo not meant for production, uses its own format, assumes 64-bit dictionary words, uniform value distribution, and large arrays, and measures steady-state throughput only. 2016 results on gcc 5.3.0, CPU model not exact. Not rerun by anyone independent. The repo now redirects to github.com/fast-pack/dictionary.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc 5.3.0 (printed in README benchmark output); Makefile sets -fPIC -O3 -march=native -std=c++11 (not stated next to the results)

notes: All claimed numbers match the README tables (Skylake size 2: 4.00 vs 1.91; size 4096: 4.14 vs 2.12; size 1048576: 11.85 vs 8.47; KNL size 2: 7.75 / 3.22 / 1.48). The record's caveat about size 8192 being slower for AVX2 was wrong and is corrected; 6.44 is the size-524288 figure. Repo moved to fast-pack/dictionary (github.com/lemire/dictionary redirects); 112 stars, Apache-2.0, last commit 2017-04-05.

tier_reason: README 'Sample output' gives first-party decode times for LEB128 vs PrefixVarint/leSQLite/leSQLite2 from the repo's own benchmark code; Makefile shows -std=c++14 -O3 but compiler and CPU are not stated, so C.
notes: Numbers match the README sample output exactly (LEB128 1.165e-03 s, PrefixVarint 5.693e-04, leSQLite 4.043e-04, leSQLite2 4.815e-04; ratios 2.047/2.882/2.420 printed by the program). README confirms 'not production quality' and UB on malicious input, and that encoding speed is not measured. 8 stars, Apache-2.0, not a fork, last commit 2018-01-22.
